restatement: Add a SECTION block ({{SECTION title level=N skip_empty=B}}...{{END_SECTION}}) to the headless core: lexer, parser, interpreter, analyze, render stats and spec. It writes a markdown heading (level clamped 1-6, default 2), a blank line and its body with leading and trailing blank lines trimmed, followed by one line break. When the body renders as whitespace only, the whole section disappears (heading and spacing included) and is counted in stats.sectionsOmitted, unless skip_empty=false keeps the heading. Bad titles and levels are type-errors at the tag, an unclosed SECTION is a syntax-error at its tag, and SECTION counts toward maxDepth. Templates without SECTION must render exactly as before, no existing test expectation may change, and no runtime dependency may be added.
brief_mismatch:
c1 says consecutive sections are separated by one blank line, but the design contract says they are separated by exactly the blank lines the template holds, with nothing added. The frozen test 'adjacent sections get no blank line added' expects '## A

a
## B

b
', with no blank line between the sections. The implementation follows the contract and the test, so c1's wording is wrong as written.

Check that package.json gains no dependency (m3).
Read the lexer and whitespace changes for any effect on templates without SECTION, and test non-SECTION errors (unclosed IF, stray END_IF) to confirm their messages and locations are unchanged (m2).

findings.title: An omitted section leaves the template's blank lines from both sides, so its neighbours end up separated by two blank lines

serves.scenario: The goal-critical question asks whether an empty section leaves no stray blank lines. Take the usual prompt layout of sections separated by one blank line: when the middle section is empty, its own tag lines vanish but the blank line before it and the blank line after it both remain. The surviving sections are then separated by two blank lines, not one, so the omission leaves visible spacing behind. The same happens between paragraphs and in a FOR loop whose iterations are separated by a blank line.

findings.rubric: Reviewer brief goal-critical question: does an empty section leave no stray blank lines, with standaloneLines on and off? Also c3: 'produces no output at all, heading and spacing included'.
evidence: test:sc-empty: own-line tags around an empty body, standaloneLines true

findings.title: A variable title containing a line break injects extra markdown structure into the heading

serves.scenario:
With a title taken from data, a value such as 'T
# Injected' produces a second top-level heading inside the prompt. The contract rejects only empty or non-string titles, so this is outside the card's criteria; it is noted as a hardening point for prompt assembly.
